articleTitle: The game PIG: making decisions based on mathematical thinking
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: A study of the game PIG can be introduced to high school or first year undergraduate students as an interesting case for the study of decision making based on ''mathematical thinking''. When a player is playing a match of this game with an opponent, at each step in the game he or she has to decide whether to ''continue'' or to ''stop''. Students can learn to develop a strategy for making such a decision, based on the ''expected gain'' and related probabilities. The strategy should also involve the examination of the total score earned from previous games as well as a comparison with the opponent's score. The purpose of this paper is to help teachers to show students how such a strategy may be developed. This study will provide students with a good example of solving problems with mathematical thinking. It can also be an interesting computer programming exercise for them to code the strategy into a computer program and see how a computer can help in decision making.

articleTitle: 'Deconstructing Rolle': a teaching proposal to foster first year undergraduates' deductive reasoning
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: (''Deconstructing Rolle'' is not a Woody Allen movie ...)Deductive reasoning is a fundamental instrument of mathematical thinking; however, students reveal serious difficulties in mastering it. A didactical model should be designed to enable undergraduates to overcome their fallacies of deductive inferences. In this paper, the mental model theory by Johnson-Laird and Byrne is proposed as a cognitive framework to analyze students' difficulties in deductive reasoning. We consider a teaching method that enables first year undergraduates to make explicit the properties tautologically implicit in the hypothesis of a theorem and to reflect on them. A contextual exploratory research is presented.

articleTitle: Follow that car! Investigating a simple class of car following model
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: A simple mathematical model for how individual vehicles follow each other along a stretch of road is discussed. The resulting first-order differential equation can be used as an application of solution techniques taught at A-level and first year undergraduate level, and as a motivator to encourage students to think critically about the physical interpretation of the results that the equation produces.

articleTitle: On torpedoes and non-intuitive problems
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: Teachers need to know problems which will shake their students' intuitions. Listed in this paper are several problems which have proved to have been successful in getting students to think about topics and notions they thought they knew. Students have not only solved the conundrums (often with help), but they have often developed them further into research projects.

articleTitle: Game theory, people power and Philippine politics
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: Though game theory has been utilized mostly in economics, it has wide applications in other fields as well. This paper delineates two illustrative game-theoretic applications to Philippine politics - the People Power Revolution in the mid-1980s and the conflict over the Spratly Islands in the mid-1990s. Zero-sum games model these two events, and elementary matrix theory is used to determine pure strategies and locate equilibrium points. Recommendations for using game theory in other political situations are included, in an attempt to bridge the gap between the classroom and the real world.

articleTitle: Raising standards in mathematics through effective classroom practice
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: Schools where pupils achieved standards significantly higher than would have been expected from their prior attainment were identified using value-added analyses which linked National Curriculum and GCSE data in mathematics to a range of input measures. Factors contributing to this high attainment were then identified through extended interviews with LEA advisors, head teachers, mathematics subject leaders and classroom teachers. These factors were triangulated at classroom level through participant observation. The factors common to the majority of schools are contrasted with findings from other projects and analysed to provide a rationale for recommended good practice.

articleTitle: Logic and the National Curriculum
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: This paper reviews the historic relation between logic and the mathematics curriculum. A list of logical elements for modern school mathematics is proposed. The current National Curriculum is checked against this list and found to be deficient, especially in relation to the development of the ideas of proof. Arguments for reform are presented.

articleTitle: Modelling traffic flow; interpreting roots and applying summations
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: A simple mathematical model for how traffic flows along a road is introduced. The consequent analysis of the model can be used as an application of techniques taught at A-level and first year undergraduate level, and as a motivator to encourage students to think critically about the physical interpretation of the results which the model produces.

articleTitle: Symmetry of the simplest Celtic step patterns
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: In this paper we describe the way in which simple square pattern Celtic designs are constructed. In particular we demonstrate the two procedures by which a simple unit is used to develop a step pattern tile. We then go on to show that up to symmetry there are in fact only three basic types of step pattern tile.

articleTitle: Rotation of coupled coordinate systems
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: Rotation of two reference frames with the common origin is considered. Each reference frame rotates about one of its axes, and they have a pair of mutually perpendicular axes. Vector algebra is used to describe the motion.

articleTitle: A graphical method for function composition
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: Function composition is an important process for creating a new function from two given functions. Students can have a difficult time understanding the notation and concept of function composition. These difficulties may arise because function composition is difficult to visualize. Here, a graphical method for composing functions is obtained through a modification of the cobweb graphical analysis technique from dynamical systems. This method has been used successfully in introductory mathematics classes to enhance students' understanding of function composition.

articleTitle: Supporting student learning
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: An electronic survey indicates that there is a wide variety of methods which are currently used in UK higher education institutions to support undergraduate learning in mathematics. This article is intended to raise awareness of what colleagues are doing and to promote an exchange of ideas.

articleTitle: Reading and writing and some basic arithmetic: using ambc zpcyigle in the classroom
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: An introduction to some of the basic techniques of cryptography is given along with examples of how cryptography can be employed in teaching mathematics and used as a cross curricular theme.

articleTitle: Modelling a barnacle goose population
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: This paper explores a number of models for the growth of a barnacle goose population. These geese spend their summers breeding in Spitsbergen and then winter in Caerlaverock on the Solway Firth. The population growth is modelled using exponential models and a variety of logistic models. The paper shows how each of the growth phases in the post-war history of this population can be related to conservation measures. Microsoft Excel spreadsheets have been used to find appropriate parameters for each of the models. The paper, and the student project it is based on, exemplify the use of modelling to generate understanding of the processes represented by raw data.

articleTitle: Mathematical needs of young employees
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: In this article we consider the mathematical needs of young employees. We interviewed both employees and their employers from a wide range of industry, commerce and the public sector. We ascertained the mathematics that is perceived by employers as being needed, as well as that actually used by employees. We also consider the use made of commercial numeracy tests and make recommendations related to the 'maths problem' in this country.

articleTitle: Flying - what you can find out with just a little bit of maths
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: The basic diagrams for the lift and drag of a wing and the lift-to-drag ratio are common in texts on aeronautics and how to fly. However, what is not normally given is the use of these diagrams to illustrate other aspects of flying - the speed required to fly straight and level (for each angle of attack of the wing) or the power required at each speed setting. This paper discusses these aspects, and grounds them in reality by using data from the Wright brothers' experiments on gliders. It also approximates the data with simple polynomial expressions, and shows that the main features of the curves derived are not sensitive to this sort of approximation. The paper uses little more than GCSE mathematics, but provides a real-life application of forces, moments and power that may appeal to many students.

articleTitle: Variations of the tiling problem
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: The usual tiling problem determines which polygons can be used to cover the plane exactly without overlaps or gaps. We consider two variations of that problem. The first attempts to determine polygons that can tile the plane by reflections as in a kaleidoscope. The second determines polygons that can be used to create polyhedral stampers that produce a tiling of the plane by rotation along any edge.

articleTitle: Propellers - just another type of wing
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: Propellers are not well understood - either in the general aviation community of in the applied maths community - even though they are, in reality, just another type of wing. This paper uses little more than A-level mathematics to illustrate how propellers work, including showing how designers choose the appropriate twist to give to the propeller blades. It thus provides an application which may appeal to many students.

articleTitle: Teaching mathematical modelling in a design context: a methodology based on the mechanical analysis of a domestic cancrusher
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: The work presents a methodology for teaching mathematical modelling skills to A-level students, typically those students engaged in A-level programmes that include mathematics, physics and design. The methodology gives an example illustrating how mathematics teachers and design teachers can take a joint perspective in devising learning opportunities that develop mathematical and design abilities concurrently. The example is situated in the context of product design and shows how mathematical modelling can be taught as an essential technique of technical product analysis and as a foundation for creativity in product design.

articleTitle: A report on experiences of using desktop video conferencing in mathematics
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: This paper reports on the results of an experiment to investigate the use of desk top video conferencing (DVC) to provide one to one tutorial support in mathematics. The paper describes how the equipment has been used and provides examples from some of the sessions that have taken place. The authors then outline the potential advantages and disadvantages of DVC in this context.

articleTitle: Comparing mathematical models of traffic flow
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: A number of distinct mathematical models of how traffic flows along a one way stretch of road are considered. Two of the models are shown to have the same mathematical structure, despite corresponding to completely different aspect of traffic flow. A further set of two models provides an example of how to introduce students to the process of making physically meaningful comparisons between models which are based on differing key variables.

articleTitle: The importance of mathematics to employers
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: While there is an underlying assumption that Mathematics is a ''basic'' value, the author considers that employers do not realize the true value of Mathematics as a base for general employment, and management in particular. Proceeding from experience with one of the country's largest employers, this article (based on a conference address) seeks to outline the benefits mathematicians can bring to an employer, whether or not they are ever expected to ''do sums''.

articleTitle: Solids through reflecting mirrors
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: This article shows how images of regular solids can be created by using reflecting mirrors and one face of the solid. It is meant to create an appreciation for the structure of solids and to introduce the principles of reflection and symmetry.

articleTitle: Exploring and interpreting expected values
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: This article explores the concept of expected value within the context of a gambling proposition known as Royal Match wagering. Royal Match wagering allows the better to win money when dealt cards of the same suit. The game is named for the hand yielding the maximum payoff, a king and queen of the same suit. Specifically, this article: (a) explains the rules of this game; (b) calculates its expected value using a standard deck of cards; (c) investigates the effects of various deck compositions on the expected value; (d) considers implications for bettors; and (e) discusses advantages of using Royal Match to teach expected value.

articleTitle: Invited review: we must not let the future be the prisoner of yesterday's ideas
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: This article discusses changing perceptions of numeracy in a changing world and puts forward arguments for integrating calculator use into the earliest years of schooling, based on the findings of work done both in this country and abroad. It also discusses the undoubted dangers of unreflective calculator use before considering how its position relates t the final report on the Implementation of the National Numeracy Strategy.
